title: feat(spec)!: retire the connector triggers array — the ConnectorTrigger shape nothing registered, polled or received (#20287)
body:
Part of #20287

Clause-②: no (narrowing). The tombstone refuses `triggers`, which parses today. `@objectstack/spec` minor with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition, as the ruling sets.

Retires `connector.triggers` (the whole `ConnectorTrigger` array) under ADR-0049, per the ruling on the card (letter B; ADR-0041 unchanged, no new ADR).

- `triggers` is a `retiredKey()` tombstone on `ConnectorBaseSchema`, so both carriers refuse it at parse and in `tsc`. The prescription names the two shapes that work today: an `api` flow for an external event and a `schedule` flow for a scheduled pull, each calling the connector's action in a `connector_action` node.
- The provider-bound refusal (`connector.zod.ts:1238-1244` at the branch point) is deleted, not re-reasoned: the tombstone refuses every value on every carrier, so the rule became unreachable, and its reason ("the provider derives them") was untrue.
- `ConnectorTrigger` leaves whole (`RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR[18]`). `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` gains `integration/Connector:triggers` and `integration/DeclarativeConnectorEntry:triggers`.
- D2 `connector-triggers-removed` (step 18, retired from the load path, lossless strip) and D3 `connector-triggers-retired`. The earlier `triggers[].interval` rename is absorbed (`spec-property-retirement` §0): `connector-health-and-trigger-durations-unit-in-key` and its unreleased D3 entry leave step 18.
- Ledger: the six `triggers` rows collapse into one `dead` tombstone row (connector dead 30 to 25, classified 60 to 55, regenerated). The README partition is corrected.
- Pins: `connector-triggers-retirement.test.ts` (16 tests). The ablation legs and gate readings are in the card report.

#20287 stays open for its action half: `actions.description` and `actions.outputSchema` go `live` after objectui#11028 and the pin bump.
